### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **5** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via assertReferencesResolve (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL), masterDetailHeadersCallerReads (symbol, a method of class ObjectQL))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 32 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7de0265fc7330cf9a830bf7f2088bc80185671ff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a54db069ddce28aa1a03a4aa3bf772e37a847155` — the merge of head `8d99c119d5833083858e9f36ca3ff1579641043a` into base `7de0265fc7330cf9a830bf7f2088bc80185671ff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a54db069ddce28aa1a03a4aa3bf772e37a847155 && git checkout a54db069ddce28aa1a03a4aa3bf772e37a847155
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7de0265fc7330cf9a830bf7f2088bc80185671ff 8d99c119d5833083858e9f36ca3ff1579641043a && git checkout -B drift-repro 7de0265fc7330cf9a830bf7f2088bc80185671ff && git merge --no-ff 8d99c119d5833083858e9f36ca3ff1579641043a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7de0265fc7330cf9a830bf7f2088bc80185671ff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7de0265fc7330cf9a830bf7f2088bc80185671ff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fef935481de0e9f967826abfc94936092f9a02b3`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #22519 (body and all eight comments; ruling 6107211425 binding; claim 6111839441; os-dev-report 6113287460), decision card #22892 (context for ③ only, not a ruling), PR #22891 (body, file list, the net diff of `origin/main...` the head: 7 files, +754 / −58, fetched into a review ref and read as objects), the head's check-runs, and on `origin/main` only `packages/objectql/package.json`, ADR-0055 §2–§3, `ObjectQL.find` with `fillQueryAstDefaults`, and `resolvePreviewParents` for comparison. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Disclosure rule kept: classes, positions and functions only.

**Check-runs at the final read:** 34 runs, no `failure`. Three still `in_progress`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)` (shards 1, 3, 5, 6 are `success`). Of the seven required contexts, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are `success`; `Lint & Repo Gates` and `Test Core` are not yet concluded. `Check Changeset` is `success`. The derived-gate families those pending runs carry (every `check:*` gate, `check:system-context-census`, `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check:durability-log-level` among them, and the two test shards) are concluded by those runs, not by this record: the owning seat arms nothing until all three read `success`, and a red among them re-opens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

**The accept-set change the diff implies — one narrowing, for non-system callers only.** A write of a master-detail detail (insert single and array, `insertMany`, update by id with or without a repoint, the predicate/bulk update) naming a header the caller's own read door does not return now answers what a header that exists nowhere answers: the reference check of the supplied `master_detail` value refuses `reference_not_found` inside `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (previously admitted), and a parent-scoped `requiredWhen` / `readonlyWhen` meets an unbound `parent` (the requirement is refused as unevaluable, the lock holds; previously judged on the unreadable header's stored state). No new error code, no status change. **Right** — this is ruling A's mechanism, read 1 then read 2, and nothing loosens.

**Every write path the ruling names takes the two-read shape — right.** Read on the head: insert (single and array) resolves `parent` through `resolveMasterDetailParents` (head `:14983`) and runs `assertReferencesResolve` per row (`:15010`); `insertMany` is `insert` with partial-row errors (`:15321`); update by id resolves the landing header through `settleMasterDetailLanding`'s `resolve` callback into `resolveMasterDetailParent` (`:16465`), the repoint's `previousParent` through the same function (`:16485`), and the reference check at `:16603`; the predicate/bulk update goes through `resolveMasterDetailParents` for landing (`:16767`) and previous (`:16779`) headers and the reference check at `:16925`. The three seams each ask `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` first (`:8953`, `:9013`, and `:8717` via `masterDetailHeaderExists`). Every remaining `referenceCheckContext` site on the head is either read 2 of those seams (`:8687`, `:8957`, `:9020`) or the pre-delete dependents probe (`:17925`), which reads no header for a write; the remaining `referenceExists` caller is the dangling-reference audit (`:9493`), not a write. None is left on the old read. Read 2 is unchanged byte for byte apart from being fed the read-door set (`$in` over `readable` instead of `ids`).

**The plain `lookup` probe is unchanged — right.** `assertReferencesResolve` picks `masterDetailHeaderExists` only on `def.type === 'master_detail'` (`:8639`–`:8641`); `referenceExists` is untouched; the control pin at new test `:332` asserts a lookup to the same object admits an unreadable id, refuses a nonexistent one, and asks no read door.

**System callers are unchanged — right.** `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` returns every asked id when `context.isSystem` (`:8750`), so read 2 runs exactly as before; `assertReferencesResolve` returns at its first line for a system context, so `masterDetailHeaderExists` is never reached by one. Pinned at new test `:447` (header bound whoever owns it, zero non-elevated header reads). The census row 29c on the system-context page states this stand-down accurately, including that a system caller's write skips the reference check altogether.

**A readable header is still judged on its stored values — right.** The read door is projected to `id` and its row contents are never consulted; read 2 is the unchanged elevated, tenant-kept read. The hide/mask control pins (new test `:413`) serve the caller a header whose state column is hidden or masked and still get `required`. The preview's per-column masking stays in `resolvePreviewParents` and is not copied — as the ruling orders.

**A failed caller read binds as missing — right, and fail-closed in the safe direction.** The `catch` in `masterDetailHeadersCallerReads` logs once at `warn` and returns an empty set; in the `parent` binding that is an unbound `parent`, in the reference check it is `false`, so `reference_not_found`. The `assertReferencesResolve` docblock now names this as the one exception to that check's fail-open and says why. It matches the preview's failed-read handling and the ruling's "a header it does not return binds as a missing header binds". Pinned for a refused read of the header object on all four reference-check doors (`:307`) and on `requiredWhen` (`:388`). `warn` is the right level: the failure is handed to the caller as a refusal, nothing claims to persist.

**The batched caller read returns every readable id for a large batch — right at the engine level.** The door read passes no `limit`; `ObjectQL.find` fills no default one (`fillQueryAstDefaults` parses only `orderBy` and `expand`, and its docblock pins that `where`, `fields`, `limit`, `offset` and `top` carry no default), so the engine's own path returns every row the caller may read for the deduplicated `$in` set. A single id is asked by equality and a batch by `$in` — the predicate shapes read 2 already sends, so no new driver capability is required. A composed middleware that injected a row cap would bound the set, but that exposure is identical to the preview's door read the ruling names as the model (`resolvePreviewParents`, same `find` shape, no `limit`); nothing in this diff adds to it.

**Pins against the ruling's list — complete.** Unreadable equals nonexistent on insert, batch insert, repoint by id and bulk repoint (reference check, both header states, message-equality with the id removed), the partial `insertMany`; `requiredWhen` on insert, update by id and bulk, repoint by id and bulk; `readonlyWhen` by id and bulk, lenient and strict; the mechanism (door, then elevated, for the binding and for the reference check). Controls: readable header unchanged; hidden or masked state column still judged stored; nonexistent id; `controlled_by_parent` detail unchanged under a readable header and taking the same rule under an unreadable one; system caller unchanged; plain lookup unchanged. The three updated pins encode the new read shape correctly: the tenant-scope pins count two header finds per resolution and assert the caller's tenant on all six reads (the door read inherits the caller's tenant like any caller read), and the cost pin counts one batched door read plus one batched elevated read per insert and one single-id door read per supplied header for the reference check.

**Public surface — none changed.** Two new `private` methods on `ObjectQL`; no export added, removed or re-typed. `@objectstack/objectql`'s entry re-exports `ObjectQL` from `engine.ts`, so the behaviour ships from the one package the changeset names. ADR-0055 is not edited (file list); the "settled upstream" docblock is rewritten to state the rule, and the four comments that described the write's header read as elevated-only are corrected — both as the ruling orders.

**Cost, noted and not a contract matter.** One id-projected caller read per header resolution (once per batch) and one per supplied `master_detail` value in the reference check (the reference check's door reads are per value, not batched); a preview with a header pays one more id read because its read 2 now carries the write's own door. Line count 812 against the ruling's 300–600 estimate, the surplus being the 496-line pin file and the census counts.

### ② Semver level

**Changeset:** `.changeset/22519-unreadable-header-write.md`, `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, body headed BREAKING (an accept-set narrowing), carrying `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its category walk, the FROM / TO statement and the one-line fix (grant the writer read on the master, or declare the detail `controlled_by_parent`). **Matches what the diff publishes:** nothing is added to the accept set (`no`), and the accept set narrows for non-system callers (`(narrowing)`, which AGENTS.md reads as BREAKING); no spec key, export or stored shape moves, so no migration prescription is owed. The one published package touched is `@objectstack/objectql`; the test files and `content/docs` publish nothing. No `skip-changeset` label (labels: `documentation`, `size/l`, `tests`, `tooling`).

**The `Clause-②:` line agrees across the three places.** PR body line 2: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Changeset: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Claim 6111839441: `Clause-②: no`, with the arm spelled on its next line as the Narrowing bullet — the same declaration, the PR body and changeset being the governing spellings. `minor` for a breaking narrowing follows the launch-window convention the changeset names and the family precedent the claim cites (#22739, #22800); `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` are reported exit 0 by the dev on this head, `Check Changeset` is `success`, and `Lint & Repo Gates` (pending) is where the repository's own reading concludes.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: none declared.

**Deviations (six), each answered:**
1. `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` edited outside the claim's declared file surface — **accepted.** `check:system-context-census` requires one row per `ExecutionContext.isSystem` read and the ruled system-caller stand-down is a new read (`masterDetailHeadersCallerReads`); row 29c is accurate (judged above) and the counts are generator output. Mechanical, gate-required, and declared; no other path leaves the surface. The conditional `plugin-security` test file was not used (item 6).
2. Shared clone deepened with a `--shallow-since` fetch of `origin/main` so `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` could answer — **accepted.** A fetch is a permitted read; it moved a shared remote-tracking ref, which the discipline names as a hazard for a sibling's moving-ref reads, not a prohibition; no file was edited.
3. Full `objectql` and `plugin-security` runs on the pre-merge commit, the merged head given typecheck plus the eleven targeted files — **accepted** under the scoped re-check rule (incoming commits touched neither package's behaviour), and moot for the verdict: the head's check-runs are the authority on the merged generation, and two `Test Core` shards plus `Lint & Repo Gates` are still pending at the final read (see above).
4. Attribution: model-free commit trailers and the session-URL PR footer, over a harness reminder asking otherwise — **accepted; this is the rule.** The seven authored commits on the branch carry the `Claude-Session` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair and no model identifier; the merge commit carries none.
5. `main` moved again after the merge and was not re-merged — **accepted.** The queue rebuilds on current `main`; no re-merge is owed before this record.
6. No `plugin-security` test-only file — **accepted.** The claim declared it conditional; the `controlled_by_parent` control is pinned in `packages/objectql` with the synthetic read scope, and the dev reports `plugin-security`'s real-rules suite (aliased to `objectql` src, the controlled-by-parent suites included) green on the pre-merge commit. The head's `Test Core` is the merged-generation reading of that.

**Out-of-scope finding (one) — escalated, held by #22892.** `ObjectQL.resolvePredicateRelated` (the #18682 one-hop related read) still reads a tenanted master elevated with no read door, and its verdict comes before the reference check, so a detail carrying a predicate rule that traverses its master-detail FK still answers an unreadable header by the header's stored state. This is a different seam from the two the ruling names (the header binding and the reference check); the diff touches it only to correct its docblock's "like `parent`" analogy. #22892 (`needs-user-decision`, `security`) carries the question of which ruling governs that read; this record takes no position on it and treats #22892's options table and its landing note as the filing seat's proposal, not a ruling. Nothing in that finding reverses anything this diff does.

**Governance:** no governed-surface path in the file list; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`; 812 changed lines, under the 3,000 line Tier H threshold; head repo equals base repo; the PR is draft and unarmed, as the claim's "one contract-review-tier review before the queue" requires. This record is that review.
